analysis:
Examined docs/reference/configuration.md (head lines 354-690; the changed lines are 553-555) and the one-line change in EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation.swift (head 457-458). The doc change adds two rows. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP covers the buffer-cache sweep on whole-Mac idleness. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION covers retention of up to min(2 GiB, grant/8) of free KV segments, reinstalled at admission, with zero-fill-on-demand host pages for new segments, plus the SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS row. Both are forwarded to the launchd job. The code change threads `environment` into the paged-KV construction call at BackendPreparation.swift:457-458, so the segmented backend now reads these controls from the injected environment instead of the process environment.

Security relevance: retained KV segments are 'uncommitted and uncharged' and are reinstalled at admission instead of freshly allocated and zero-filled, which touches T-028 (residual inference data in GPU/KV memory across requests). The documentation says new segments use zero-fill-on-demand host pages or device zero-fill, but the patch excerpt does not show whether a reinstalled retained segment is cleared before another request reads it. That would matter for cross-tenant leakage between requests. The segment retention and reinstall code (EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm or refute this. I raise no finding, but the next pass should verify that retained segments are either zeroed or never exposed beyond the initialised length (paged attention masks) on reinstall.

The environment-injection change itself adds no new attack surface visible here. The controls are not new trust-boundary inputs, since the operator is already in the TB-003 adversary set. No auth, encryption, attestation or billing paths were touched. The doc's claim that the memory-pressure reclaim signal is shortfall-gated is unverified.
